new.description: the door's own cases — the streams it arms by default, and the two classes it splits

summary: the CLI's closed-output door is pinned at the function: both streams armed by default, the reader-gone class quiet, every other stream error still loud
acceptance: narrowing the default arming to stdout alone, or widening the quiet class to swallow every stream error, reds a case: the door is driven directly over emitters it is handed, and the loud arm — a stream error outside the reader-gone class still reaching the uncaught-exception path — has a case of its own
pins: quietOnClosedOutput ends a reader-gone error quietly on each stream it is handed
quietOnClosedOutput re-raises a stream error that is not the reader going away
quietOnClosedOutput arms stderr beside stdout when it is handed no streams
notes: Build note: the three shipped cases drive the door through `status` at spawn level, so stderr's arming and the re-raise arm are pinned by nothing — narrowing the arming to stdout, or to one verb, reds nothing today. The re-raise lands on `process.nextTick`; capture it with a case-scoped `uncaughtException` listener, never a global one (`platform-facts.md`, *vitest's JSON reporter can claim success over a non-zero exit*).
